pr_title: Allow fragments to override the name of new profiles
pr_body:
After this commit we only set the default fields of a profile - primarily the
name field - as late as possible, after layering has already completed.
This ensures that we pick up any modifications from fragments.

## PR Checklist
* [x] Closes #12520
* [x] I work here
* [x] Tests added/passed

## Validation Steps Performed
* Add a fragment at
  `%LocalAppData%\Microsoft\Windows Terminal\Fragments\Fragment\fragment.json`
  with
  `{"profiles":[{"updates":"{61c54bbd-c2c6-5271-96e7-009a87ff44bf}","name":"NewName"}]}`
* Windows PowerShell profile is created with the name "NewName" in settings.json ✅

issue_context.title: Partners cannot rename a template via fragment plugins
issue_context.body:
### Windows Terminal version

_No response_

### Windows build number

_No response_

### Other Software

_No response_

### Steps to reproduce

Ship a template fragment with something like:
```
"profiles": [
      {
        "updates": "{f184b75f-6c82-5ea5-9b3e-3203d66c5f82}",
        "name": "My new profile name",
      },
    ]
  }
```
Then restart the terminal to take the new fragment in account.

### Expected Behavior

"My new profile name" should appear as the profile name

### Actual Behavior

The old name still appears, "name" in case of "update" is discared.

The rationale here is to replace the generated named in WSL, which is using the registered WSL ID (`Ubuntu2004LTS` for instance) instead of the Display Name registered (and used as the tab name entry) like the more readable `Ubuntu 20.04 LTS`.
Other kind of entries are overridden by the fragment, but not the `name` one.

The workaround right now is to hide the generated template with `hidden: true` and add a whole new entry.
comments:
Huh. It should be able to do that. Why doesn't that work? I bet this regressed in one of the many settings refactors over the last few months. 

Thanks for filing this! Let's make sure to get this fixed.
I'll debug this issue starting next week. 🙂

The problem here is that fields in a user's settings.json take precedence over fragments. Since profiles are created and written with a "name" field, the "name" field in fragments usually has no effect. If you were to remove the "name" field from your settings.json this would work as expected.

What is unexpected however is that we don't respect such updates when the dynamic profile is first added. I'm going to submit a PR for that.

:tada:This issue was addressed in #12627, which has now been successfully released as `Windows Terminal v1.12.1098`.:tada:

Yes, temporarily at least.

> Is it _correct_ to copy the name up to the user-owned leaf node?

You mean the profile that gets written into settings.json? Yeah, this is equivalent to the previous code and the old code before the refactorization.

> What caused this bug originally? The user-owned leaf node wasn't being assigned a name, was it? Or, was it being assigned a name too early?

Assigning a name too early.

----

The rather lengthy comment in `_addUserProfileParent` explains this somewhat... hopefully.
This code is executed whenever we encounter a new user profile - one that truly doesn't exist yet in the user's settings.json. In these cases we'll make a new, empty child profile and insert it as a user profile. The `profile` given as a parameter to `_addUserProfileParent` is the first parent of our new user profile (hence the function name).

However unlike the old code, we shouldn't simply call `CreateChild()` here. Under the assumption that the given profile has a finalized inheritance, `CreateChild()` copies the name and hidden fields over into the child. If we add more parents to our user profile however (fragments basically), then the value for name and hidden might change still. Due to this we'll have to defer copying any attributes for as long as possible and can't use `CreateChild()` which would do it early.

The way we detect these new user profiles is that they don't have an origin yet.
I thought about adding another attribute to Profile, saying that it's not finished initializing yet, but I felt like that's just as bad of a hack.
